description: Cases built to fool PatchAhead. Every one of these is either a defect the prototype actually had, or a way its successor could plausibly acquire the same defect. `expect_patched` and `expect_reported_only` are `path:line` sites; anything patched that is not in `expect_patched` is a false positive, which is the failure mode this suite exists to catch. Cases carrying `known_gap` are ones a correct tool passes and this one does not: they are in the dataset on purpose, scored honestly, and fail the build the day they start passing.

cases.note: The prototype's headline defect. `order` and `customer` both carry a `total`; only one was renamed.

files.app/a.py:
def revenue(order, customer):
    return order["total"] - customer["total"]

cases.note: `analytics` is a different object that happens to expose the same method name.

files.app/a.py:
def go(client, analytics):
    return client.fetch_orders(), analytics.fetch_orders()

cases.note: A bare string literal is not a field access and must not even be reported.

files.app/a.py:
# the total field is renamed
LABEL = "total"
DOC = "see order['total'] in the docs"


def f(order):
    """Read order['total']."""
    return order["total"]

cases.note: AST columns are UTF-8 byte offsets; slicing a str with them corrupts the line.

files.app/a.py:
def f(order):
    name = "José"
    label = "λ"; emoji = "🚀"
    return name, label, emoji, order["total"]

cases.note: The hardest column case: multi-byte characters between the line start and the edited span.

files.app/a.py:
def f(client):
    return client.fetch(label="café ☕", timeout_seconds=5)

cases.note: Walking the outer function used to find the inner loop as well, matching it twice and emitting overlapping edits.
A method on a nested class is its own scope and must be reported with its own dotted symbol.
Comprehensions and lambdas are expressions in the enclosing statement, not separate scopes to skip.

files.app/a.py:
def f(orders, order):
    squares = [order["total"] for _ in orders]
    get = lambda: order["total"]
    return squares, get

cases.note: Decorators and async must not confuse scope tracking or range calculation.
A keyword argument several lines below the call's opening paren.
Running twice must be a no-op, not a second rename.

files.app/a.py:
def f(order):
    return order["amount"]

cases.note: One module migrated, one not. Only the stale one may change.
Two of four modules mention the name; only one is a real access on the owner.

files.app/a.py:
def f(order):
    return order["total"]

cases.note: The repository owns this function; renaming its call sites would break it.
A non-constant key cannot be shown to be the renamed field.
The page variable is logged, so replacing it with a cursor would change behavior.

files.app/a.py:
def sync(api, log):
    page = 1
    out = []
    while True:
        r = api.get(page=page)
        out.extend(r["items"])
        log.info("page %d", page)
        if page >= r["total_pages"]:
            break
        page += 1
    return out

cases.note: `socket.connect` takes a `timeout_seconds` too; it is not the renamed one.

files.app/a.py:
def f(client, sock):
    a = client.fetch_orders(timeout_seconds=5)
    b = sock.connect(timeout_seconds=9)
    return a, b

cases.note: `retries` is an ordinary word, and `send_email` belongs to another library entirely. With no function named in the change document there is nothing to tell the two calls apart, so neither is rewritten and both are reported. This handler used to rewrite both -- reachable from any structured change document that omitted the function, and from a markdown one as soon as the classifier learned to read this shape.
`self.order` is the declared owner; `self.cache` is not.
A receiver scraped from a vendor's example is a hint, not a constraint: `api_client` is the same SDK call.

files.app/a.py:
def f(api_client):
    return api_client.fetch_orders()

cases.note: Comments, blank lines and alignment must survive a range edit untouched.

files.app/a.py:
def f(order):
    # keep this comment

    value = order["total"]   # and this trailing one

    return value

cases.note: Impact is not a single-file property. Three modules, three qualifying sites, one plan.

files.app/a.py:
def a(order):
    return order["total"]

cases.note: Four syntactic matches on one field name in four lines, with four different verdicts. The module-level string is not a candidate at all: it is never a subscript, a `.get()`, or an attribute, so it is filtered by syntax rather than by scoring.

files.app/mixed.py:
LABEL = "total"


def summarize(order, customer, rows):
    a = order["total"]
    b = customer["total"]
    c = rows[0]["total"]
    d = order.get("total")
    return a, b, c, d, LABEL

cases.note: The same call spelling in two modules. One imports it from the SDK; the other defines it. Renaming calls to the repository's own function would break it rather than migrate it, so ownership of the name decides, not the spelling of the call.
`import analytics as a` puts a one-letter name in front of the renamed method. It is not the receiver the change document names, and a short alias is not a reason to assume it is.

files.app/alias.py:
import analytics as a


def go(client):
    client.fetch_orders()
    a.fetch_orders()

cases.known_gap: the loop variable `o` is an `order`, but showing that needs alias analysis over the iterable; PatchAhead reports the site and declines to patch it (roadmap PR #8)
cases.note: The dominant known false negative, written down as an executable case rather than left out of the dataset. Under-migrating is survivable -- a missed site is fixed by hand -- but it is still a miss, and it stays visible in the benchmark until it is fixed.

cases.known_gap: `current = order` is a one-line alias inside a single function; resolving it needs local dataflow PatchAhead does not do (roadmap PR #8)
`self._order` is assigned in `__init__` and read in another method; connecting them needs cross-method attribute tracking (roadmap PR #9)
`factory.get_client()` returns a client, but knowing that needs return-type information PatchAhead does not have (roadmap PR #8)
